title: Real-time Collaborative Inventory Tracking
business: Retailers managing high-velocity stock across distributed warehouse locations.
problem: Legacy relational databases struggle with high-frequency updates and the overhead of polling for state changes, leading to stale inventory data and overselling.
solution: Firestore provides a serverless document database with realtime client synchronization capabilities, allowing inventory dashboards to update instantly as stock levels change without manual refresh cycles.
steps: Initialize the Firestore client within the warehouse management application.
Define a document structure where each unique item ID maps to a document containing stock counts.
Implement listeners on the client side to subscribe to document snapshots for specific inventory categories.
Update document fields via the client SDK when stock movements are scanned.
Leverage the automatic synchronization to push updates to all connected dashboard clients.
outcome: Warehouse staff gain immediate visibility into stock levels across all locations, significantly reducing the risk of overselling due to data latency.
limitation: The realtime synchronization model can lead to high read costs if listeners are attached to excessively large collections; verify this by monitoring the number of document reads in the Cloud Console.

questions.question: In Real-time Collaborative Inventory Tracking, why is Firestore preferred over legacy relational databases?
options: It eliminates the need for manual polling to see inventory updates.
It provides lower storage costs for relational data.
It forces all users to refresh their browsers simultaneously.
It requires a fixed schema for all inventory items.
questions.explanation: Firestore's realtime synchronization capabilities allow dashboards to update automatically, removing the need for polling.
questions.evidence: Firestore provides a serverless document database with realtime client synchronization capabilities, allowing inventory dashboards to update instantly as stock levels change without manual refresh cycles.

questions.question: In Real-time Collaborative Inventory Tracking, what is a primary operational risk when using realtime listeners?
options: The database will automatically delete old documents.
Excessive read costs if listeners are attached to large collections.
The system will fail if more than two users connect.
Realtime updates are only available for relational data.
questions.explanation: The documentation notes that attaching listeners to large collections can lead to high read costs, which is a key tradeoff.
questions.evidence: The realtime synchronization model can lead to high read costs if listeners are attached to excessively large collections; verify this by monitoring the number of document reads in the Cloud Console.
